facts.raw_span: 2 months of progressive proximal muscle weakness
difficulty combing her hair and rising from a chair
morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
dysphagia for solids and liquids
without fever or weight loss
symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in the upper limbs and 3/5 in the lower limbs
brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
leukopenia (WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL)
microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL)
elevated C-reactive protein (18.8 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (109.2 mm/hr)
bilateral sacroiliitis
bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement

concepts.why: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and bilateral sacroiliitis are consistent with JDM, a rare autoimmune disease.
Suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and markedly elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies suggest thyroiditis, an inflammatory condition of the thyroid gland.
Morning stiffness, symmetric muscle weakness, and bilateral sacroiliitis are consistent with RA, a chronic autoimmune disease.
Overlap of musculoskeletal, rheumatologic, and endocrine symptoms suggests MCTD, a condition characterized by a combination of autoimmune features.
Bilateral sacroiliitis is a distinct clinical entity, often associated with inflammatory back pain and stiffness.
Progressive muscle weakness and bilateral thigh intramuscular edema suggest myositis, an inflammatory condition of the muscles.
Suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and elevated inflammatory markers suggest thyroid storm, a life-threatening complication of untreated hyperthyroidism.
Microcytic anemia and elevated inflammatory markers suggest AIHA, an autoimmune condition characterized by the destruction of red blood cells.

rationales.F01: Progressive proximal muscle weakness is a hallmark of Juvenile Dermatomyositis and Myositis.
rationales.F03: Morning stiffness is a common symptom of Rheumatoid Arthritis and Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
rationales.F05: Absence of fever and weight loss makes Thyroid Storm less likely.
rationales.F08: Leukopenia can be seen in various autoimmune diseases, including Mixed Connective Tissue Disease and Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia.
rationales.F09: Microcytic anemia can be seen in Chronic Diseases, including Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia.
rationales.F10: Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicate significant inflammation, consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis, Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, and Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F11: Bilateral sacroiliitis is a characteristic feature of Sacroiliitis and can be seen in other spondyloarthropathies.
rationales.F12: Bilateral thigh intramuscular edema with enhancement is consistent with Myositis.
